props.title: A jazz band for a Colorado wedding, from the ceremony to the last dance.
props.lede: You know that feeling in a great little jazz club, when the band sounds amazing and you can still talk to the person next to you? We can bring that to your wedding with a jazz band that grows through the day, from one or two musicians at the ceremony to four for the dancing.

headingText.html: You can book the band for one part of your day or all of it, and one person on our team will look after you the whole way through. Want something other than jazz? Learn more about our wedding music.

props.title: How a wedding jazz band grows through the day

rows.text: A solo jazz guitarist or a duo can play ballads while your guests find their seats, the processional you choose, and something upbeat for the walk back up the aisle.

Upright bass and guitar make a lovely duo for cocktail hour, at a volume that’s easy to talk over. Jazz standards are a great choice here, since they’re the songs a lot of people already know and love.

For dinner, we add drums to make a trio, and the drummer plays with brushes to keep the volume soft. The band can stop for each toast, so your speaker doesn’t have to compete with the music. Changes Jazz Trio is another great option for dinner.

rows.term: The first dance and the dance floor
rows.text: For the dancing, we add a horn or a singer to make a quartet, and the band can play the swing and soul side of the standards. Later on, the DJ can take over on the same sound system.

props.html: You can see the standards we play, and plenty more, in our full song list.

props.title: Which jazz band is right for your wedding?

rows.text: We’ll start with upright bass and guitar, add drums if you’d like them, and let you know which musicians are playing when you book. This is the one to book if you care more about the sound than about a particular name.

This trio plays jazz standards with a modern edge on guitar, fretless bass (a bass with a smooth, singing tone) and drums. We can add a saxophone to make a quartet for the dance floor. And with Changes Jazz Trio, you’ll know exactly who’s playing before you decide.

rows.term: Jazz until dinner, then something else
rows.text: If you’d like jazz standards through dinner and pop and rock for the dancing, we can pair our jazz musicians with a cover band like Tejas Singh or with the DJ.

props.html: Wondering about prices? We break it down size by size in what a jazz band costs in Denver. Getting married in Colorado Springs or Vail? Learn more about the venues and the drive for Colorado Springs and Vail.

props.title: What couples ask about wedding jazz bands.

items.q: Which size of jazz band does a wedding reception need?
items.a: It depends on what’s happening at that point in the reception. The size of your venue matters, too, and for a ballroom of two hundred, we’d put a singer out front. Tell us the guest count and the venue and we'll recommend the size. Signet Artists books wedding jazz bands across Denver and the Colorado mountains.

items.q: How loud is a jazz band at a wedding?
items.a: At the ceremony and through cocktail hour, it’s gentle enough for your guests to greet each other over it. At dinner, the band stays at about the level of the conversation at your tables. For the dancing, the quartet can play like a real dance band, up to whatever your venue allows.

items.q: Will a jazz band play our first dance?
items.a: Yes. If the song is a standard, it's probably already on our song list. If it isn't, send us the title with your date and we can usually learn it.

items.q: Is a jazz band the right choice if we want dancing at our wedding?
items.a: It can be, if your guests love dancing to swing and soul standards.

props.title: Send us the date and the venue, and we'll size the jazz band to your day.
props.lede: We’d love to play your wedding, whether you want one jazz guitarist or a full quartet, and we’ll make sure the sound system is right for your venue.
